store.niche: geothermal mapping and sensing, the technologies for finding and characterizing new geothermal resources (subsurface imaging, geophysics, machine-learning prospecting, drilling-data analytics), not geothermal power in general

quotes.text: By combining exclusive data on the subsurface of the region with AI-driven analysis, the company identified a promising new drilling site, striking what has now become the most productive pumped geothermal well in the U.S.
They are Fervo Energy, Zanskar Geothermal, AlterG Resources, Quaise Energy and the University of Utah.
Geothermal Radar is developing a digital modeling system that connects subsurface and industrial data with geothermal models for real-time simulation, valuation, and feasibility assessment.

Thermofilic, led by CEO Sebnem Duzgun, has created an artificial intelligence-based prediction system that supports investment decisions in geothermal energy by using remote sensing data and other data types to scan large areas that produce accurate and targeted footprints of potential subsurface geothermal resources.
The company is supported by Good Growth Capital, Ameren, NSF-SBIR, and DOE ARPA-E.
GSP specializes in risk assessment and analysis across all phases of geothermal project development.
Developer Quaise Energy was awarded up to $25 million in funding from DOE to advance its superhot geothermal power plant, 50-MW Project Obsidian, in Central Oregon.
Three Houston-based companies—Fervo Energy, Quaise Energy and XGS Energy—have been selected by the U.S. Department of Energy to advance geothermal technologies and field tests.

The company’s technology combines autonomous drilling and advanced subsurface modeling, substantially increasing the speed and space efficiency of geothermal projects, enabling the use of geothermal HVAC in dense, urban locations.
They are Fervo Energy, Zanskar Geothermal, AlterG Resources, Quaise Energy and the University of Utah.
Geothermal startup, Zanskar, has used AI to discover a hidden geothermal reserve underneath the desert in western Nevada.

US geothermal technology company XGS Energy Inc has been selected by the Department of Energy (DOE) for funding to drill a deep appraisal well in New Mexico in one of 21 projects tapped to win a federal grant for field tests and exploration of geothermal sources across the United States.
GSP specializes in risk assessment and analysis across all phases of geothermal project development.
